hints: Remember that speed and total amount are controlled by two different things, concentration for rate and total moles for yield.
Work out moles of HCl each time using moles = concentration x volume in dm3, you get 0.025 mol first and 0.030 mol second.
Compare the concentrations for collision frequency with the total moles for how much $\text{CO}_2$ can form, then put the two trends together.
walkthrough:
**Spot who runs out first**

Marble chips ($\text{CaCO}_3$) are in large excess, so hydrochloric acid is the limiting reagent. That means all the product comes from the acid.

$$\text{CaCO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{CaCl}_2 + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Decide the rate from concentration**

Rate depends on how crowded the acid particles are, not on total volume. The second experiment uses $0.5 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ instead of $1.0 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ at the same temperature.

Lower concentration means fewer collisions per second, so the reaction is slower.

**Decide the total product from moles**

Total product depends on total moles of the limiting reagent:
$$\text{moles} = \text{concentration} \times \text{volume (in dm}^3\text{)}$$

First: $1.0 \times 25/1000 = 0.025 \text{ mol HCl}$

Second: $0.5 \times 60/1000 = 0.030 \text{ mol HCl}$

**Put it together**

Second experiment is slower because concentration is lower, but makes more $\text{CO}_2$ and other products because there are more total moles of acid to react. That is slower rate with greater final yield.

options.A: Incorrect. More products is right because 0.030 mol > 0.025 mol, but faster is wrong. Rate follows concentration (0.5 is lower than 1.0), not total volume.
options.B: Incorrect. Faster is wrong and less is wrong. Students choosing this confuse total volume with concentration, thinking 60 cm3 means faster and stronger.
options.C: Correct. Lower concentration of 0.5 mol dm-3 gives fewer successful collisions per second so the rate is slower. Larger total moles of 0.030 mol HCl gives more products when the limiting acid is all used up.
options.D: Incorrect. Slower is right, but less is wrong. This trap comes from thinking lower concentration must mean less product, forgetting to calculate total moles where volume matters.
